          How to read this

          Fuel surcharges are a percentage of transportation charges. Changes are in percentage points (diesel in dollars). Red means fuel costs went up, green means they went down. "—" means no published rate for that week.

          About these documents

          Every link opens the carrier's, USPS's or the regulator's own copy. Each carrier opens to its next and last earnings call, then one drop-down per year with the documents and earnings reports for that year; "Effective" and "Updated" dates are read from the document itself, checked Oct 9, 2026. Some carriers replace a file at the same address when they update it, so the dates show the version we last checked.

          The bird this thing is named for

          The original express courier. Still undefeated on attitude

          Before the internet, the fastest thing in logistics had feathers. For 3,000 years, "expedited shipping" meant strapping a note to a bird — and it delivered. No address. No app. Just knew where it was going, and got there before anything else could.

          That bird would not be impressed by today's mail. Because here's the dirty secret of parcel shipping: the sticker rate is a decoy. Fuel adjustments, residential fees, "extra handling," peak-season charges — the real bill is buried in the fine print, and it changes every January whether you're ready or not.

          The carriers count on you finding out late. The bird's whole trick was finding out first. That's the job here: every rate change, surcharge and service alert, caught early and delivered straight — no fluff, no waiting for someone to forward you the memo.

          So the mark in your corner isn't a mascot. It's a job description: carry what matters, directly, first. Occasionally late. Always faster than a fax.

          • Speed50–60 mph
          • Range600 miles, further when annoyed
          • PayloadA leg band. No tracking number
          • Record3,000 years. Still racing

          — Coop

          Abridged from the usual almanacs. Corrections to the bird.
